newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Tsang starts budget speech with autonomy pledge.
newsitem.headline: Tsang starts budget speech with autonomy pledge.

text.p: Hong Kong Financial Secretary Donald Tsang kicked off his annual budget speech on Wednesday with a detailed reiteration of how the territory was guaranteed an autonomous economic policy after it reverts to China.

The Basic Law, drawn up by Beijing to act as Hong Kong's constitution following the British colony's handover to China, stated Hong Kong shall maintain independent finances, manage economic policy according to law and keep its free trade system.

"These articles have a clear message. The resources of Hong Kong are to be managed separately and independently -- they are to be used exclusively for the benefit of Hong Kong people," Tsang said in his 1997/98 budget address to the legislature.
"Hong Kong's finanical and monetary affairs shall be determined exclusively by Hong Kong law.
"And third, trade and investment shall continue to enjoy freedom of movement and freedom of markets," he said.
Because the budget for the fiscal year starting on April 1 straddles the transition at midnight of June 30, it was prepared in consultation with Beijing, Tsang noted.
But Beijing has stated that, from July 1, preparation of Hong Kong's budget would be the business of Hong Kong alone, he stressed.
